# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**[Your mailing address]**
**[City, State, ZIP]**
**[Your phone number]**
**[Date of this letter]**

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana
Member Appeals
**[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]**

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-06**
- **Member:** Reese Iverson
- **Member ID:** W233165693
- **Reference number:** POC-757C3B7E16-21498
- **Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
- **Plan:** Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana (Commercial/ACA), State of Louisiana
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 (HTML), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/ (effective 2025-11-15)

---

## 1. What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery. I am asking the plan to overturn that decision and approve the procedure.

The notice states that the request was denied because the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. My records show a documented course of conservative care that ran far longer than the duration the plan's own published guideline uses as its conservative-care threshold, and I am asking that those records be reviewed again in full.

## 2. The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

The criteria identified in connection with my denial come from the Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 guideline. That guideline states:

> "Irregular joint surfaces Glenoid sclerosis Osteophyte changes Flattened glenoid Cystic changes in the humeral head Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks’ duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes) Hemiarthroplasty Hemiarthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:"

The same guideline also states:

> "Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months’ duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) *Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:"

The measures of adequacy the plan's own guideline uses are **at least 6 weeks' duration** of conservative management and **at least 6 months' duration** of pain and loss of function that interferes with daily activities. My records meet and exceed both:

| The plan's published measure | What my records document |
|---|---|
| Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration | **16 weeks** of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, from 2026-02-24 to 2026-06-16, with 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |
| — additional conservative measures | NSAIDs for **8 months** with inadequate relief; corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-30 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief |
| Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months' duration that interferes with daily activities | **18 months** of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest; I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side |
| Limited range of motion on physical examination | Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain |

My imaging of 2026-07-07 (MRI of the shoulder) shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. My records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status. The corticosteroid injection in my record was given on 2026-03-30, several months before the request at issue.

In short: the plan's guideline sets six weeks as the relevant conservative-care duration, and my chart documents sixteen weeks of supervised therapy plus eight months of anti-inflammatory medication and an injection, all before surgery was requested. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

## 3. Please send me the specific criteria that were applied to CPT 29827

I want to be straightforward about one thing: the criteria quoted above, which are the criteria identified with my denial, are the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline's shoulder **arthroplasty** criteria. The procedure my surgeon requested is a rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. Apart from the language quoted above, I have not been given the specific criteria the reviewer applied to my procedure, and I am not going to guess at or paraphrase policy text I have not been shown.

I am therefore requesting, in writing, a copy of the exact clinical review criteria — the guideline title, section, and the specific conservative-care requirement — that the reviewer applied to CPT 29827 in my case, together with the reviewer's credentials. The plan holds those criteria; I do not. Carelon publishes its Joint Surgery, Spine Surgery, and Small Joint Surgery guidelines free of charge with no login, so providing the exact section applied to my request should be a simple matter. If the conservative-care standard actually applied to my procedure differs from the six-week measure quoted above, I ask that it be identified specifically so that my records can be compared against it point by point.

## 4. What I am requesting

I ask that the plan:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-06 (reference POC-757C3B7E16-21498) and authorize the rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician in orthopedic surgery who has my complete record, including the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-02-24 through 2026-06-16 and the MRI report of 2026-07-07; and
3. Send me, in writing, the specific criteria described in Section 3 above.

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window stated in the notice; my appeal must be received by **2027-02-02**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. Any other member may also call the number on the back of their insurance card to ask where member appeals are filed.

Enclosed are: **[list what you are enclosing — e.g., copy of the denial notice, physical therapy discharge note, MRI report of 2026-07-07, office notes from Dr. Duval, medication records]**.

Thank you for taking a second look at my records. Please contact me at **[your phone number]** or **[your email address]** if anything further is needed.

Sincerely,

**Reese Iverson**
Member ID: W233165693
Date of birth: **[your date of birth]**
Group number: **[group number, if listed on your card]**
**[Signature]**

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
